questions.text: In this lesson’s MRTR workflow, how does a server obtain required client input without sending an independent request to the client?

options.A: It stores a callback in the HTTP connection and invokes it later.
options.B: It returns input_required with embedded input requests; the client fulfills them and retries the original operation.
options.C: It changes the original request ID into a persistent protocol session ID.
options.D: It treats the client’s capability declaration as the completed input response.

questions.explanation: MRTR expresses missing input as a result. The client obtains the requested input and makes a new independent request repeating the original operation with inputResponses and requestState.

questions.text: The lesson seals requestState with HMAC. A valid token was issued for one principal and one set of arguments. Why must the server still check those bindings on retry?

options.A: Because HMAC automatically expires all tokens at the next request.
options.B: Because the client must be allowed to replace the token’s principal.
options.C: Because a valid signature alone does not prevent reuse in the wrong request context.
options.D: Because HMAC encrypts arguments but leaves principal names unsigned.

questions.explanation: Integrity proves the state was not altered, but principal, method, argument digest, and expiry checks restrict where and when an unchanged token may be accepted.

questions.text: In run_mrtr(), the loop continues while resultType is input_required, increments request_id each round, and has no round counter. What happens if a modified server always returns a fulfillable input_required result?

options.A: It stops after three rounds because request_id enforces a budget.
options.B: It rejects the fourth response because all tokens expire after three requests.
options.C: It exits after the first input response because the request ID changes.
options.D: It keeps retrying because the loop has no explicit round limit.

questions.explanation: The demo’s normal state machine finishes, but run_mrtr itself has no enforced round budget. Incrementing IDs provides correlation, not a stopping condition.
